title: An analog ac voltage amplifier based on a single straintronic magnetic tunnel junction
authors: Cael Johnson, Rahnuma Rahman, Supriyo Bandyopadhyay
abstract: Magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) are known for their digital applications (memory and logic). A special class of them called "straintronic" magnetic tunnel junctions (s-MTJ) has lately emerged as a potential platform for analog applications because their conductance can be varied continuously with mechanical strain generated with a gate voltage. The conductance versus gate voltage (transfer) characteristic always has a linear region and that can be leveraged for a variety of analog applications. Here, we discuss one such application, namely analog voltage amplification. If the s-MTJ's gate voltage is fixed around the midpoint of the linear region and a small ac voltage is superimposed on it, then the ac voltage can be amplified without distortion as long as its amplitude is small enough to avoid gate voltage excursion beyond the linear region. Unlike a transistor-based voltage amplifier whose amplification is determined solely by the transistor's internal parameters - namely the transconductance and Early resistance - here the amplification can be varied by an external power supply voltage. We examine the maximum allowed amplitude and frequency of input signal for distortion-free amplification by modeling the magnetization dynamics and derive an expression for the amplification.
summary: This paper proposes using straintronic magnetic tunnel junctions (s-MTJs) as a tunable analog AC voltage amplifier. The device's conductance is controlled by strain via an applied gate voltage, allowing for linear operation in specific regimes. The key finding is that the amplification gain can be externally tuned by adjusting the bias supply voltage.
main_problem: To demonstrate and analyze the potential of straintronic magnetic tunnel junctions (s-MTJs) as a novel analog AC voltage amplifier.
main_result: The s-MTJ can function as an analog amplifier whose gain is tunable by an external supply voltage, unlike traditional transistor amplifiers.
method: Theoretical modeling involving the Landau–Lifshitz-Gilbert-Langevin (LLGL) equations to analyze magnetization dynamics under superimposed AC gate voltages.
model_or_system: The physical system is a straintronic Magnetic Tunnel Junction (s-MTJ), whose conductance is continuously modulated by mechanical strain induced via an external gate voltage ($V_G$).
key_observables: Amplification factor ($	ilde{V}$ proportional to $v_g$), conductance swing, and the maximum allowed input signal amplitude before distortion.
important_parameters: The amplification factor is proportional to the supply voltage ($V_s$); operating frequency is limited by magnetization dynamics (GHz range).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the AC gate voltage excursion remains within the analytically derived linear region of the s-MTJ's transfer characteristic.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the s-MTJ structure, its conductance vs. $V_G$ transfer curve highlighting linearity, and time-domain simulations showing signal amplification and frequency limitations.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the s-MTJ as an analog platform, derives the linear conductance dependence on $V_G$, models the AC voltage amplification using LLGL dynamics, and discusses tunability and operational limits.
why_interesting: While primarily condensed matter/spintronics, the analysis of non-linear dynamic response (magnetization precession) to small signals, coupled with external circuit tuning, touches upon concepts relevant to open quantum systems and sensing mechanisms.
